newsitem.title: UK: Steady rain finally falls on parched UK crops.
newsitem.headline: Steady rain finally falls on parched UK crops.

text.p: Britain's parched farming areas are finally seeing some rainfall which may give grain and sugarbeet crops a much-needed soaking, weather experts and farming sources said on Friday.
"The more disturbed weather patterns which we predicted are coming true," said a spokesman at the Meteorological Centre.
In East Anglia, one of Britain's main crop areas, persistent drizzle was reported with about three mm measured so far in Norwich, the centre of the region.
"It's fairly persistent and it's wetting the ground quite well," said an official at Norwich Weather Centre, adding that rain had been falling since around dawn.
Steady rain was also reported in the Bristol and Wiltshire areas in the west of England.

The rain is forecast to move in an northeasterly direction during the course of the day, although Britain's south and far northeast could see some drier interludes. The east would remain cold until Saturday.
"We've got some more (rain) coming in across the country tomorrow (Saturday)," said a spokesman at the London Weather Centre.
"It's going to stay fairly mobile for the next few days with fronts crossing the coutnry at various points, nationwide," he said.
Farming sources have said rain was needed not just for crops in the ground, but also to replenish reservoirs which were low after a dry winter.
